A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same G-Designer study. Their text, equations, figures, tables and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching material relocated into v3's expanded appendices.

before.justification: v2 reports original six-benchmark evaluations, communication-cost measurements, adversarial tests, topology case studies and ablations in Table 1 and Figures 4–7.

after.justification: v3 retains original benchmark evaluations and reports additional efficiency, component-ablation, memory and scalability results in Tables 2, 3, 5 and 6.

M1.justification: The node encoder, task-specific virtual node, VGAE, two-stage topology decoder, regularization objectives and policy-gradient optimization remain unchanged. Appendix A retains the same algorithm; newly ablating existing components does not introduce a method change.

E1.justification: The six datasets and three task families remain unchanged. However, v3 Table 3 extends adversarial evaluation to GSM8K, whereas v2's reported attack and component-ablation experiments concern MMLU. This modestly broadens adversarial test coverage.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains exactly the same comparators. Within the scalability comparison, v3 Table 6 adds Complete Graph alongside Chain and GPTSwarm, whereas v2 Figure 7's sensitivity comparison includes only Chain and GPTSwarm against G-Designer.

E3.justification: v3 replaces the 3–9-agent sensitivity curve with a GPT-3.5 evaluation at 5, 10 and 20 agents. It adds separate training/inference resource measurements and memory evaluation up to 1,000 agents. The stated optimization budget also changes from 40 queries to 40 or 80, without specifying their allocation or establishing that retained results were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 Figure 7 ablates sparsity regularization and the anchor topology. v3 Table 3 additionally ablates the node encoder and task virtual node, reporting clean and attacked results on MMLU and GSM8K. Tables 2, 5 and 6 substantially extend efficiency and scaling analyses beyond the earlier token-cost plots and agent-count curve.

E5.justification: Neither version reports evaluation seeds, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals or significance tests. The retained sampling parameter M = 10 concerns method optimization, rather than uncertainty reporting for experimental results.

E6.justification: Table 1's scores are unchanged, but v3 adds resource measurements and expanded ablation results and replaces the earlier scalability results. Examples include 3.8 GB memory at 1,000 agents and, in Table 6, 77.82% MMLU accuracy for G-Designer versus GPTSwarm's 75.38% with 20 GPT-3.5 agents. These are newly reported settings, not same-setting gains over v2.

T1.justification: The MACP objective, graph construction, generative-model equations, nuclear-norm argument and optimization derivation are retained. Changes to definition numbering and notation do not alter the mathematics; no new proofs or formal assumptions are introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same central contributions: MACP and an effective, task-adaptive, robust topology designer. The headline accuracy, token-saving and robustness claims remain unchanged. Additional experiments support these claims without redefining them.

C2.justification: v3 newly attributes performance gains to adaptive topology design rather than the anchor alone, interprets task-node removal as disrupting adaptiveness, and discusses larger-scale efficiency. Its new Impact Statement also asserts harmless outputs conditional on an aligned base LLM, without accompanying safety-test evidence. These extend interpretation without changing the central explanatory framework.

D1.justification: v3 adds dataset test counts and licenses, the GPT-3.5 checkpoint identifier, and training/inference timing information. Conversely, it removes v2's explicit five-way self-consistency setting and task-specific AutoGen configurations. The code link and most core implementation settings remain unchanged; newly supplied dataset counts do not establish changed splits.

R1.justification: v3 removes the web/social/trade/transport-network motivation and associated citations, and prunes other references such as STOP and COReX. Related-work descriptions are shortened, but the central positioning against input-independent multi-agent topologies remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 substantially condenses related work and baseline explanations, replaces the RQ/numbered-observation organization with consolidated Main Results and Framework Analysis sections, and reorganizes supporting material into Appendices B–D. It also adds an Impact Statement and revises the author and affiliation block.

P2.justification: The publication layout is comprehensively reformatted. v2 Figure 7 is replaced by expanded tabular analyses, resource and dataset tables are added, and the original case-study Figure 4 moves to the appendix as Figure 6. The retained token-cost and attack plots become Figures 4 and 5; these relocations are not new experimental content.

improvement.justification: The added efficiency and scalability measurements and tests of the node encoder and task node strengthen v2's narrower empirical validation. This provides a modest net improvement, tempered by removed baseline configuration details, incomplete allocation of the revised 40/80-query budget, and an unsupported safety assurance in the new Impact Statement.
